title: Hybrid latency vs cost curation - scheduler notes
content:
Goal:
Evaluate a hybrid scheduler heuristic that explicitly trades off 95th/99th tail latency against per-token GPU cost for mixed customer workloads. We want practical knobs that map to SLO budgets (ms) and cost budgets ($/M tokens) instead of only batch size/timeouts.

Background/context:
- Many service routes have a dual objective: keep p95 < 120ms for spikes, but maintain cost < $X per M tokens. Current continuous-batching heuristics tune timeouts and max-batch but don't expose cost-aware gating.
- Hypothesis: adding a decay-priority factor per-cohort (decay on age + recent throughput) and a cost-pressure multiplier (derived from token-rate vs cost-target) improves tail latency without blowing cost for steady-state throughput.

Experiment design:
1) Implement scheduler flag: --hybrid-curation=true that computes a per-queue score S = priority*exp(-age/alpha) * (1 + cost_pressure*beta).
2) cost_pressure = clamp((observed_cost_rate / cost_target) - 1, -0.5, +2.0).
3) alpha sweep: [50ms, 200ms, 500ms], beta sweep: [0.2, 0.6, 1.2], max_batch caps: [32, 64, 128].
4) Workloads: "chat-burst" (many small requests; lambda spikes), "assistant-long" (few long seqs), and mixed 60/40 split. Inject microburst spikes (10x QPS for 2s) every 60s.

Metrics collected:
- p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (server side), token-per-second throughput, GPU utilization, avg batch size, GPU tokens / $ metric (normalized).
- fairness: fraction of requests that wait > target_timeout (SET per-route).

Preliminary results (subset):
Route: chat-burst (alpha=200ms, beta=0.6, max_batch=64)
- baseline (no hybrid): p95=210ms, p99=375ms, avg_batch=11, GPU_util=42%, cost_norm=1.00
- hybrid-curation: p95=135ms, p99=230ms, avg_batch=26, GPU_util=61%, cost_norm=1.09
Notes: tail improved ~35% at ~9% cost increase. Significant smoothing of microburst tail spikes.

Route: assistant-long (alpha=50ms, beta=1.2, max_batch=32)
- baseline: p95=140ms, p99=260ms, avg_batch=44 (because long seqs pile), GPU_util=78%, cost_norm=1.00
- hybrid-curation: p95=150ms, p99=275ms, avg_batch=38, GPU_util=72%, cost_norm=0.96
Notes: slight latency regressions but cost improved by prioritizing smaller batches. Suggest per-route defaults for long-context routes to avoid regressions.

Observations and takeaways:
- cost_pressure knob effectively throttles batch growth when the observed cost rate exceeds the target; this prevents runaway batching on high-throughput routes.
- decay on age helps reduce head-of-queue starvation for low-rate tenants and reduces p99 in bursty scenarios.
- sweet spot for mixed workloads: alpha ~150-250ms, beta ~0.5-0.8, max_batch ~64. This gave balanced p95 improvement with <10% cost increase.
- fairness: some low-priority cohorts saw waiting times increase; need fairness guardrail that demotes cost_pressure when a request ages beyond a hard SLO.

Operational notes / runbook snippets:
- Triggering the experiment: rollout via feature-flag gate in canary pool only. Monitor these dashboards: realtime/scheduler/hybrid-curation, infra/gpu/cost-normalized.
- Quick rollback: set --hybrid-curation=false or set cost_target very high to effectively disable cost_pressure.
- Danger signals: p99 spike > 2x baseline OR cost_norm > baseline * 1.25 sustained for 5m -> rollback.

Open questions / next steps:
- Automate cost_target derivation from billing signals (coarse first, refine per-customer).
- Evaluate multi-tier cost_pressure where enterprise routes can have higher cost budgets.
- Add explicit fairness cap: ensure no request waits longer than hard_max_age (e.g., 800ms) by forcing flush.
- Run longer 24h soak under production traffic on a dedicated canary shard with A/B weight 20/80.

Quick links and commands used:
- perf harness: ./tools/run_harness --profile=burst-mix --routes=chat-burst,assistant-long --duration=30m --flag hybrid-curation=true --alpha 200 --beta 0.6 --max-batch 64
- trace extractor: ./tools/trace-agg --input /tmp/harness-traces --filter "route=chat-burst" --quantiles p50,p90,p95,p99

Notes to reviewers: this is an early synthesis; please comment on whether per-route defaulting logic should live in the control plane config or be derived online from traffic. Also weigh in on acceptable cost uplift thresholds (is 10% OK for a 35% p95 improvement?).

Priya (on behalf of serving-runtime)
